pages.content:
The Stone Age (Part 1)

The Stone Age in India marks the beginning of human civilization. It is divided into three periods:

  • Paleolithic (Old Stone Age)
  • Mesolithic (Middle Stone Age)
  • Neolithic (New Stone Age)

Humans were primarily hunters and gatherers during this time.

The Stone Age (Part 2)

Tools & Weapons:
Early humans used quartzite to make tools. These tools were rough and heavy.

Later, in the Neolithic period, they started using polished and sharp tools.

Introduction to Harappa

The Indus Valley Civilization (IVC) was a Bronze Age civilization (3300–1300 BCE). It extended from modern-day Northeast Afghanistan to Pakistan and Northwest India.

Town Planning

The most remarkable feature was its urban planning. The streets cut each other at right angles (Grid System).

The drainage system was very advanced and covered with bricks.

Decline of IVC

There are many theories about the decline:

  • Recurring Floods
  • Drying up of the Saraswati River
  • Aryan Invasion Theory

Arrival of Aryans

The Vedic Age (1500–600 BCE) marks the transition from urban to rural civilization. The Aryans came from Central Asia.

The main source of information is the Rig Veda (the oldest religious text).

Vedic Literature

There are four Vedas:

  1. Rig Veda: Collection of hymns.
  2. Sama Veda: Book of melodies and chants.
  3. Yajur Veda: Rituals and sacrifices.
  4. Atharva Veda: Spells and charms.

Society & Economy

Society: Initially tribal (Janas), later divided into 4 Varnas (Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Shudras).

Economy: Their main occupation was cattle rearing (pastoral) and agriculture. The cow (Gau) was considered the most valuable asset.
